decisions.name: Arch Hang
decisions.reason: Scapular hang hold; no hanging hold of this kind is in the library.

instructions_en: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip and straight arms.
Pull your shoulder blades down and back and lift your chest, arching the upper back without bending your elbows.
Hold the arched position while breathing steadily, then relax to a dead hang.

decisions.name: Dumbbell Around The World
decisions.reason: Same dumbbell around-the-world.

decisions.name: Assisted Squat
decisions.reason: Holding a support for balance; a regression of the free bodyweight squat.

instructions_en: Stand facing a sturdy rack or post, holding it lightly at chest height, feet shoulder-width apart.
Sit your hips back and down as deep as you can, using your hands only for balance.
Drive through your feet to stand, letting your legs do the work rather than your arms.

decisions.name: Back Extension
decisions.reason: Same bodyweight back extension.

decisions.name: Barbell Behind The Neck Press
decisions.reason: Strict press without leg drive; the library only has the behind-the-neck push press.

instructions_en: Sit or stand with a barbell across your upper back, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Press the bar straight up until your arms lock out, keeping your head neutral.
Lower under control to the base of your neck, only as far as your shoulder mobility allows.

decisions.name: Cable Bent Over Row
decisions.reason: Two-handed bar row at a low pulley; the closest match is single-arm.

instructions_en: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley, step back and hinge forward with a flat back and soft knees.
Row the bar toward your lower ribs, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades.
Extend your arms slowly while holding the hinged position.

decisions.name: Machine Bent Over Row
decisions.reason: Same lever bent-over row machine.

decisions.name: Barbell Bicep Curl
decisions.reason: Same barbell curl.

decisions.name: Cable Bicep Curl
decisions.reason: Same standing cable biceps curl.

decisions.name: Dumbbell Bicep Curl
decisions.reason: Same dumbbell biceps curl.

decisions.name: EZ-Bar Bicep Curl
decisions.reason: Same EZ-bar curl.

decisions.name: Dumbbell Box Squat
decisions.reason: Dumbbell squat to a box or bench.

decisions.name: Barbell Cable Twist
decisions.reason: Contradictory name (barbell cable twist); cannot be identified.

decisions.name: Cable Twist
decisions.reason: Contradictory name (cable twist with bodyweight); cannot be identified.

decisions.name: Machine Cable Twist
decisions.reason: Contradictory name mixing cable and machine; cannot be identified.

decisions.name: Machine Calf Press on Seated Leg Press
decisions.reason: Calf press on a leg press machine.

decisions.name: Barbell Chest Fly
decisions.reason: Not a real exercise; a chest fly cannot be done with a barbell.

decisions.name: Dumbbell Chest Fly
decisions.reason: Same flat dumbbell fly.

decisions.name: Barbell Chest-Supported Row
decisions.reason: A barbell row lying prone on a bench is the seal row.

decisions.name: Machine Chin Up
decisions.reason: Machine chin-up is the lever assisted chin-up.

decisions.name: Barbell Concentration Curl
decisions.reason: Same barbell concentration curl.

decisions.name: Crow Pose
decisions.reason: Yoga arm-balance pose rather than a gym exercise.

decisions.name: Dead Hang
decisions.reason: Two-handed hang; the library only has the one-handed hang.

instructions_en: Grip a pull-up bar overhand with hands about shoulder-width apart.
Lift your feet and hang with arms fully straight and a firm grip, body still.
Hold for time with steady breathing, then step down under control.

decisions.name: Deadlift
decisions.reason: A deadlift with no load is not a meaningful exercise.

decisions.name: Barbell Deadlift High Pull
decisions.reason: Conventional-stance pull from the floor to the chest; only a sumo version exists.

instructions_en: Stand with the bar over midfoot and grip it just outside your knees, back flat.
Lift as in a deadlift, then extend your hips explosively and pull the bar to chest height, elbows high.
Lower the bar to your hips, then to the floor under control.

decisions.name: Trap Bar Deficit Deadlift
decisions.reason: Standing on a platform adds range; the deficit variant of the trap bar deadlift.

instructions_en: Stand on a stable low platform inside the trap bar and grip the handles at your sides.
Brace, push the floor away and stand up tall, keeping your back flat.
Lower the bar to the floor under control in the same back position.

decisions.name: Elliptical Machine
decisions.reason: Same elliptical machine.

decisions.name: Flat Knee Raise
decisions.reason: Bent-knee lying raise on a bench; differs from the straight-leg lying raise and the hanging knee raise.

instructions_en: Lie on a flat bench holding its edge behind your head, legs extended just off the end.
Bend your knees and draw them toward your chest, curling your hips slightly off the bench.
Extend your legs back out slowly without letting your lower back arch.

decisions.name: Flat Leg Raise
decisions.reason: Same flat bench lying leg raise.

decisions.name: Front Lever Row
decisions.reason: Same row from the front lever position as wger's Front lever pull-up.

decisions.name: Cable Front Squat
decisions.reason: Cable-loaded front squat; no cable squat exists in the library.

instructions_en: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and hold it at your shoulders, elbows high, facing the stack.
Step back slightly, set your feet shoulder-width apart and squat down with your chest up.
Drive through your feet to stand, keeping the bar fixed at your shoulders.

decisions.name: Smith Machine Front Squat
decisions.reason: Smith machine front squat.

decisions.name: Dumbbell Glute Bridge
decisions.reason: Dumbbell-loaded floor bridge; the library only has the barbell version.

instructions_en: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, a dumbbell resting across your hips.
Hold the dumbbell in place and drive through your heels until your body is straight from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower slowly.

decisions.name: Cable Glute Kickback
decisions.reason: Cable glute kickback, which is always single-leg.

decisions.name: Machine Good Morning
decisions.reason: Machine good morning is the lever seated good morning.

decisions.name: Cable Hammer Curl
decisions.reason: Cable hammer curl with the rope.

decisions.name: Cable Hanging Leg Raise
decisions.reason: Contradictory name; a hanging leg raise is not done on a cable.

decisions.name: Hip Abductor
decisions.reason: Bodyweight form of the seated machine abduction is not an identifiable exercise; side-lying versions exist.

decisions.name: Cable Hip Abductor
decisions.reason: Same cable hip abduction.

decisions.name: Machine Hip Abductor
decisions.reason: Same seated hip abduction machine.

decisions.name: Hip Adductor
decisions.reason: Bodyweight form of the seated machine adduction is not an identifiable exercise; side-lying version exists.

decisions.name: Cable Hip Adductor
decisions.reason: Same cable hip adduction.

decisions.name: Machine Hip Adductor
decisions.reason: Same seated hip adduction machine.

decisions.name: Hip Thrust
decisions.reason: Same unloaded hip thrust with the upper back on a bench as ExerciseDB's Bench Hip Extension.

decisions.name: Machine Hip Thrust
decisions.reason: Dedicated hip thrust machine; the library only has the barbell hip thrust.

instructions_en: Sit in the hip thrust machine with your upper back on the pad and the belt or pad across your hips.
Drive through your heels to extend your hips until your torso is level with your thighs.
Pause and squeeze your glutes, then lower slowly to the start.

decisions.name: Barbell Incline Bench Press Wide Grip
decisions.reason: Wide grip on an incline bench; the closest match is the flat wide-grip press.

instructions_en: Lie on a bench set to 30-45 degrees and grip the bar well outside shoulder-width.
Lower the bar to your upper chest with your forearms vertical.
Press the bar back up over your shoulders until your arms are straight.

decisions.name: Cable Incline Chest Fly
decisions.reason: Same incline cable fly.

decisions.name: Dumbbell Incline Chest Fly
decisions.reason: Same incline dumbbell fly.

decisions.name: Dumbbell Incline Chest Press
decisions.reason: Same incline dumbbell press.

decisions.name: Incline Row
decisions.reason: A bodyweight incline row is the inverted row.

decisions.name: Dumbbell Iso-Lateral Chest Press
decisions.reason: Dumbbells already work each side independently; this is the dumbbell bench press.

decisions.name: Dumbbell Iso-Lateral Row
decisions.reason: 'Iso-lateral' names a machine; the dumbbell version is too ambiguous to identify.

decisions.name: Jumping Jack
decisions.reason: Same jumping jack.

decisions.name: Kipping Pull Up
decisions.reason: Uses a hip-driven swing to finish the rep; a distinct technique from strict or weighted pull-ups.

instructions_en: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than your shoulders.
Swing from an arched to a hollow body position, then snap the hips up and pull your chin over the bar.
Push away from the bar on the way down and flow straight into the next swing under control.

decisions.name: Kneeling Ring Ab Rollout
decisions.reason: Kneeling rollout on rings; different apparatus from the barbell and wheel rollouts in the library.

instructions_en: Set gymnastic rings low, kneel behind them on a pad and hold one ring in each hand with arms straight.
Brace your abs and let the rings travel forward and up as your hips and torso extend in one line.
Go only as far as your lower back stays neutral, then pull the rings back to the start.

decisions.name: Knees to Elbows
decisions.reason: Knees travel all the way to the elbows; a longer range than the Hanging Knee Raise.

instructions_en: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip and arms straight.
Brace your abs, curl your pelvis up and lift your knees until they touch your elbows.
Lower your legs under control without swinging before starting the next rep.

decisions.name: Barbell Legs Up Bench Press
decisions.reason: Feet off the floor removes leg drive and arch; a recognised bench press variant.

instructions_en: Lie on a flat bench and lift your feet, resting them on the bench end or holding them up with knees bent.
Unrack the bar with a grip slightly wider than your shoulders and lower it under control to your mid chest.
Press back to lockout while keeping hips and upper back on the bench, with no leg drive.

decisions.name: Lunge
decisions.reason: Same bodyweight forward lunge as candidate wger-1324 (Bodyweight lunge).

decisions.name: Cable Lunge
decisions.reason: Forward lunge loaded by a low cable; no cable lunge exists in the library.

instructions_en: Attach a D-handle to a low pulley, hold it at one side and stand tall a step away from the stack.
Step forward into a lunge and lower until both knees bend to about 90 degrees, front knee over the toes.
Push through the front foot to return to standing, then repeat on the same side or alternate.

decisions.name: Barbell Lying Bicep Curl
decisions.reason: A lying barbell biceps curl is the prone high-bench curl already in the library.

decisions.name: EZ-Bar Lying Bicep Curl
decisions.reason: Same prone high-bench curl; an EZ-bar instead of a straight bar does not make a separate exercise.

decisions.name: Machine Lying Bicep Curl
decisions.reason: Equipment permutation with no standard lying biceps curl machine; machine curls are covered by Machine Bicep Curl.

decisions.name: Negative Dip
decisions.reason: Eccentric-only dip, a named progression; the library has only full dips.

instructions_en: Jump or step to the top of parallel bars with arms locked and shoulders pulled down.
Lower yourself slowly, taking three to five seconds, until your shoulders are just below your elbows.
Put your feet down, climb back to the top position and repeat.

decisions.name: Negative Pull Up
decisions.reason: Eccentric-only pull-up, a named progression; differs from strict and weighted pull-ups.

instructions_en: Use a box or a jump to get your chin above the bar, holding it with an overhand grip.
Lower yourself slowly, taking three to five seconds, until your arms are fully straight.
Step back onto the box to return to the top before the next rep.

decisions.name: Dumbbell Overhead Press
decisions.reason: Standing dumbbell overhead press is the library's Standing Dumbbell Press.

decisions.name: EZ-Bar Overhead Press
decisions.reason: Same standing overhead press; using an EZ-bar instead of a straight bar is not a material change.

decisions.name: Dumbbell Overhead Squat
decisions.reason: Dumbbells held locked out overhead; differs from Dumbbell Squat and the barbell Overhead Squat.

instructions_en: Press two dumbbells overhead and lock your elbows, standing with feet about shoulder width apart.
Keep the weights stacked over your shoulders and sit down into a deep squat with your chest up.
Drive through your feet to stand while holding the arms locked overhead.

decisions.name: Machine Pistol Squat
decisions.reason: Not a real machine exercise; equipment permutation of the pistol squat (Smith Machine Pistol Squat already exists).

decisions.name: EZ-Bar Preacher Curl
decisions.reason: The library's Preacher Curl is the EZ-bar preacher curl.

decisions.name: Barbell Press Under
decisions.reason: Slow press-under drill; differs from the dip-and-drive Snatch Balance and Heaving Snatch Balance.

instructions_en: Rest the bar behind your neck with a wide snatch grip and set your feet in your squat stance.
Press against the bar to push yourself down into an overhead squat, locking your arms as you reach the bottom.
Hold the bottom briefly with the bar stable overhead, then stand up.

decisions.name: Dumbbell Reverse Curl
decisions.reason: Same dumbbell reverse curl; library name only adds 'Standing'.

decisions.name: Dumbbell Reverse Grip Concentration Curl
decisions.reason: Same seated reverse-grip dumbbell concentration curl as candidate edb-0403.

decisions.name: Reverse Hyperextension
decisions.reason: Same reverse hyperextension; doing it unloaded does not make a separate exercise.

decisions.name: Cable Reverse Lat Pulldown
decisions.reason: Reverse lat pulldown is the underhand-grip pulldown already in the library.

decisions.name: Barbell Reverse Lunge
decisions.reason: Same barbell reverse lunge as candidate wger-1830 (Barbell Step Back Lunge).

decisions.name: Reverse Lunge
decisions.reason: Same bodyweight reverse lunge as candidate wger-1102 (Alternate back lunges).

decisions.name: Cable Reverse Lunge
decisions.reason: Backward step against cable resistance; differs from Cable Lunge, which steps forward.

instructions_en: Hold a D-handle from a low pulley at one side and stand tall facing the stack, a step away.
Step one foot back and lower until the back knee nearly touches the floor, keeping your torso upright.
Push through the front heel to bring the back foot forward to the start.

decisions.name: Dumbbell Reverse Lunge
decisions.reason: Reverse lunge and rear lunge are the same exercise with dumbbells.

decisions.name: Reverse Plank
decisions.reason: Face-up hold on hands and heels; a different position from the face-down Plank.

instructions_en: Sit with legs straight and hands planted just behind your hips, fingers pointing toward your feet.
Press through palms and heels to lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulders to ankles.
Squeeze your glutes and hold without letting the hips sag, then lower down.

decisions.name: Ring Ab Rollout
decisions.reason: A full ring rollout from the feet is the library's Suspended Fallout; rings versus straps is not material.

decisions.name: Ring Row
decisions.reason: Ring row is the suspended inverted row already in the library; rings versus straps is not material.

decisions.name: Cable Rowing
decisions.reason: This is the rowing machine (ergometer), already in the library as Rowing, Stationary.

decisions.name: Dumbbell Russian Twist
decisions.reason: Same Russian twist; holding a dumbbell only adds load.

decisions.name: Barbell Safety Squat Bar Squat
decisions.reason: Uses the cambered safety squat bar, a distinct apparatus from the straight-bar back squat.

instructions_en: Set the padded safety squat bar on your upper back and hold its handles in front with both hands.
Brace and sit down between your hips until your thighs reach at least parallel, keeping your chest up.
Drive through your whole foot to stand, resisting the bar's pull to tip you forward.

decisions.name: Barbell Seated Front Raise
decisions.reason: Seated barbell version; library front raises are standing with dumbbells or a plate.

instructions_en: Sit upright on the end of a bench holding a barbell on your thighs with an overhand, shoulder-width grip.
Keeping your arms nearly straight, raise the bar in front of you to shoulder height.
Lower it slowly back to your thighs without leaning back.

decisions.name: Machine Seated Leg Press
decisions.reason: Seated leg press is the standard Leg Press already in the library.

decisions.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press Parallel Grip
decisions.reason: Same seated neutral-grip dumbbell shoulder press as candidate edb-0404.

decisions.name: Shrimp Squat
decisions.reason: Single-leg squat with the rear foot held behind; a different exercise from the two-legged Bodyweight Squat.

instructions_en: Stand on one leg, bend the other knee and hold that foot behind you with the same-side hand.
Lower slowly until the back knee lightly touches the floor, keeping your weight over the standing foot.
Drive through the standing foot to return to the top without pushing off the back knee.

decisions.name: Barbell Side Hip Abductor
decisions.reason: No recognisable barbell side hip abduction; source equipment permutation.

decisions.name: Side Hip Abductor
decisions.reason: Same side-lying hip abduction as candidate edb-0710 (Side Hip Abduction).

decisions.name: Machine Side Hip Abductor
decisions.reason: Machine hip abduction is already in the library as Thigh Abductor.

decisions.name: Side Lying Clam
decisions.reason: Same side-lying clam as candidate wger-1823 (Clamshell).

decisions.name: Single Leg Bridge
decisions.reason: Same exercise as Single Leg Glute Bridge.

decisions.name: Barbell Single Leg Calf Raise
decisions.reason: Impractical to balance a barbell on one leg for calf raises; single-leg calf raises are loaded with dumbbell, cable or machine.

decisions.name: Cable Single Leg Calf Raise
decisions.reason: Same exercise as candidate edb-1376 (Cable Standing One Leg Calf Raise).

decisions.name: Machine Single Leg Calf Raise
decisions.reason: One leg on the standing calf machine; library machine calf raises are two-legged and the hack version uses another machine.

instructions_en: Stand under the shoulder pads of a standing calf machine with the ball of one foot on the platform edge.
Lower the heel for a full stretch, then rise as high as you can onto your toes.
Pause at the top, lower slowly and finish all reps before switching legs.

decisions.name: Single Leg Deadlift
decisions.reason: Same bodyweight single-leg Romanian deadlift as candidate wger-1388.

decisions.name: Single Leg Glute Bridge On Bench
decisions.reason: Working foot on a bench adds range and hamstring demand compared with the floor Single Leg Glute Bridge.

instructions_en: Lie on your back with one heel on a flat bench, knee bent about 90 degrees, and the other leg raised.
Drive through the heel on the bench to lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulders to knee.
Squeeze the glute at the top, then lower your hips slowly to just above the floor.

decisions.name: Single Leg Glute Bridge Bent Knee
decisions.reason: Only the free leg's position differs; same single-leg glute bridge.

decisions.name: Single Leg Glute Bridge Straight Leg
decisions.reason: Only the free leg's position differs; same single-leg glute bridge.

decisions.name: Single Leg Hip Thrust
decisions.reason: Same bodyweight single-leg hip thrust as candidate wger-1913 (Unilateral Hip Thrust).

decisions.name: Machine Single Leg Hip Thrust
decisions.reason: One-leg version on a hip thrust machine; Machine Hip Thrust is two-legged.

instructions_en: Set up in a hip thrust machine with the pad across your hips and your upper back on the backrest.
Plant one foot on the platform, lift the other and drive your hips up until fully extended.
Squeeze the glute at the top, lower slowly and finish all reps before switching sides.

decisions.name: Barbell Sling Shot Bench Press
decisions.reason: Requires a Sling Shot elastic band device, which the library excludes.

decisions.name: Dumbbell Snatch
decisions.reason: A dumbbell snatch is done one arm at a time; same as candidate edb-3888 (Dumbbell One Arm Snatch).

decisions.name: Machine Squat
decisions.reason: Too generic to identify which machine; specific squat machines (hack, V-squat, pendulum, Smith) are already in the library.

decisions.name: Cable Standing Row
decisions.reason: Same standing cable row as candidate edb-0234.

decisions.name: Cable Standing Row Close Grip
decisions.reason: Close-grip standing cable row is the V-bar standing row in candidate edb-0234.

decisions.name: Cable Standing Row Rear Delt, Horizontal, With Rope
decisions.reason: Same standing rope rear-delt row as candidate edb-0233.

decisions.name: Step up
decisions.reason: Unloaded step-up; the library has only barbell, dumbbell and knee-raise step-ups.

instructions_en: Stand facing a sturdy box or bench and place one whole foot on top.
Drive through the top foot to stand fully on the box without pushing off the back leg.
Step down with control on the same leg and repeat, or alternate legs.

decisions.name: Barbell Stiff Leg Deadlift
decisions.reason: Same exercise as Stiff-Legged Barbell Deadlift.

decisions.name: Barbell Sumo Deadlift High Pull
decisions.reason: Wide stance with a narrow grip; differs from the conventional-stance Deadlift High Pull.

instructions_en: Stand in a wide stance with toes turned out and grip the bar with hands close together inside your legs.
Extend your hips and knees explosively, then pull the bar close to your body to chin height, elbows high.
Lower the bar to your hips and then to the floor under control.

decisions.name: Dumbbell Superman
decisions.reason: Same superman; holding light dumbbells only adds load.

decisions.name: Support Hold
decisions.reason: Same top-of-dip support hold as candidate wger-1808 (Parallel Bar Hold).

decisions.name: Toes To Bar
decisions.reason: Lifting straight legs from a hang until the feet reach the bar is the library's Hanging Pike.

decisions.name: Cable Torso Rotation
decisions.reason: Standing horizontal cable torso rotation is the library's Cable Russian Twists.

decisions.name: Tuck Front Lever Row
decisions.reason: Tucked-knee regression of the front lever row with much easier leverage.

instructions_en: Hang from a bar or rings and lift into a tuck front lever, knees to chest and torso horizontal.
Holding the horizontal tuck, pull the bar toward your lower chest by driving your elbows back.
Lower back to straight arms with control without letting your hips drop.

decisions.name: Vertical Row
decisions.reason: A steeper-angle regression of the inverted row, not a separate exercise.

decisions.name: V Up
decisions.reason: A V-up is the library's Jackknife Sit-Up.

decisions.name: Dumbbell V Up
decisions.reason: Same V-up (Jackknife Sit-Up); holding a dumbbell only adds load.

decisions.name: Wall Handstand
decisions.reason: Wall-supported static hold; differs from a freestanding handstand and from Handstand Push-Ups.

instructions_en: Place your hands shoulder-width apart a short distance from a wall and kick up until your heels rest on it.
Lock your elbows, push the floor away and tuck your ribs so your body forms a straight line.
Hold the position, then step down with control one leg at a time.

decisions.name: Wide Row
decisions.reason: Wide grip shifts the work toward the upper back and rear delts; the library Inverted Row uses a standard grip.

instructions_en: Lie under a bar set at about waist height and grip it overhand, well wider than your shoulders.
Hold your body straight from heels to head and pull your chest to the bar with elbows flared.
Lower until your arms are straight while keeping your hips from sagging.

decisions.name: Wrist Roller
decisions.reason: Same exercise as Wrist Roller.
